questions.q: How does governance differ from security in an analytics platform?
options: They mean exactly the same thing
Governance covers ownership, approved content, change control, and lifecycle, in addition to who can see data
Governance only concerns passwords
Governance only applies to Tableau Desktop
questions.explain: Security restricts access; governance manages ownership, trust, change, and lifecycle of analytics assets.

questions.q: In CRM Analytics app sharing, which role can also control who else has access?
options: Viewer
Editor only
Guest
Manager
questions.explain: Viewers use content, Editors change it, and Managers can also manage sharing, so Manager should be limited to true owners.

questions.q: Why grant app access to groups, roles, or permission sets instead of individuals?
options: Individual grants are not possible
It speeds up dashboards
Access then follows the organization structure instead of decaying as people change jobs
It removes the need for row-level security
questions.explain: Group-based grants are easier to maintain and audit; row-level security is still a separate requirement.

questions.q: What is a sound change-management path for analytics content?
options: Edit dashboards directly in production
Develop and test with real user access first, then promote with a supported method and record the change
Publish first and fix problems when users complain
Delete the old version before testing the new one
questions.explain: Develop, test, promote keeps production deliberate and reversible.

questions.q: What is the recommended approach to retiring unused analytics assets?
options: Archive first, notify owners, and delete later based on scheduled usage reviews
Delete anything not opened yesterday without notice
Never retire anything
Move them to a personal app
questions.explain: Unused assets cost refresh time and can still expose data, so retire them carefully and reversibly.
